sections.heading: What I bring to a 3D product

items.title: Seeing where a product falls short
items.body: I read the limits of what is already on the market, then improve on them so the product works better in use.

items.title: Reading new needs
items.body: I look for needs society has not answered yet and turn them into a concrete design direction.

items.title: Materials and production
items.body: I source materials and propose a production route that fits, including when the budget is tight.

items.title: Prototyping
items.body: I build real prototypes to test dimensions, handling and feel before anything goes into production.

sections.heading: Behind the drawings
sections.lead: Meet the person behind these drawings, a quick look into my world.
body: I graduated in Industrial Design from Văn Lang University. My way of working leans on product analysis and honest research.
Away from the workstation I throw ceramics, draw by hand, stitch leather, and spent a couple of years teaching drawing to children. Each one taught me a different way of reading form.
I treat every project as a chance to balance how a thing looks against how it works. Three words I like: try, learn, fix.
